summary: A denial-of-service flood attack occurred against host-01 from ip-01 targeting ip-02, with a second flood occurring shortly after.

sequence.description: User-01 logged into host-02 at 13:16, which may have enabled access to a system that could be used to launch attacks on host-01.
A denial-of-service flood attack began against host-01 at 13:24 from ip-01 targeting ip-02.
A second denial-of-service flood attack occurred against host-01 at 13:30 from ip-01 targeting ip-02.

findings.statement: A denial-of-service flood attack occurred against host-01 from ip-01 targeting ip-02.
A second denial-of-service flood attack occurred against host-01 from ip-01 targeting ip-02.
The remote login event on host-02 may have allowed user-01 to establish a persistent session, which could have enabled the subsequent DoS attacks on host-01.

recommendations: Investigate the remote login event on host-02 to determine if user-01 had legitimate access and whether it was authorized. Why: The remote login on host-02 precedes the DoS attacks on host-01, and user-01 is present in both events, suggesting a possible connection between the login and the attack. Less disruptive option: Review the login logs for host-02 without immediately revoking user-01's access to determine if the login was legitimate.

Verify the source of the traffic from ip-01 to ip-02 and confirm whether it is a known legitimate service or a malicious actor. Why: Both DoS flood events originate from the same source ip-01 and target the same destination ip-02, indicating a consistent attacker pattern. Less disruptive option: Temporarily block ip-01 at the firewall without disrupting legitimate traffic from known sources.
uncertainty: It is unknown whether the remote login on host-02 was legitimate or part of an attack vector. (would be settled by: The logs do not show whether user-01 had legitimate access to host-02 or whether the remote login was authorized.) The role of user-01 in the DoS attacks is not established; the user may have been compromised or may have initiated the attacks. (would be settled by: There is no data on whether the DoS attacks were initiated by user-01 or by a separate entity.) Limitations: The events do not show whether user-01 had legitimate access to host-02 or whether the remote login was authorized. There is no evidence of file access, process execution, or lateral movement from host-02 to host-01. The attack type is labeled as DoS in both flagged events, but no evidence is provided about the source of the traffic or the intent behind the floods.
